title: Import skills from an agent plugin
description: Run a local web app, sign in to Glean with OAuth, upload a Claude Code, Codex, or Agent Skills plugin, and publish every skill it contains through the Skills API.

codeWalkthrough.intro: One command starts a small web app on your computer. The app signs you in with the official @gleanwork/auth package, reads the plugin you upload or point it at, finds its skills the way agent harnesses do, and publishes each skill folder as one ZIP bundle with the official SDK. Glean never needs access to the plugin's repository.

examples.title: Sign in with the official CLI
examples.description: The Sign in button runs the glean-auth binary from the pinned @gleanwork/auth package, the same command as npm run login. It registers an OAuth client dynamically and opens Glean's approval page. The app checks the session with createGleanTokenProvider and never handles the credentials itself.

examples.title: Find skills the way agent harnesses do
examples.description: Read marketplace files for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, then each plugin's manifest and its skills/ folder. Without a manifest, look in the standard skills folders, then search the whole tree. Remote plugin sources, commands, agents, hooks, and MCP servers are reported rather than imported.

examples.title: Validate, plan, and publish
examples.description: Upload each distinct skill folder once. Validate every bundle without saving it, flag invalid skills and name conflicts, show which names already exist, and skip skills whose published files already match. Then create each selected skill once, without automatic retries.

examples.title: Serve the app on this computer only
examples.description: The server listens on 127.0.0.1, answers only to its own host name, and requires the session key from the link it prints. That keeps other websites open in your browser from driving the importer.

prerequisites: Node.js 22.12.0 or newer, and a browser on the same computer
A Glean instance with Skills enabled
Your Glean backend URL, usually https://your-company-be.glean.com
Permission to create skills, using the SKILLS OAuth scope or the SKILLS permission on a user-scoped token
A local copy of the plugin: a cloned repository, a plugin folder, or a zip of either

demoQueries.query: Sign in, then run a test import
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: After sign-in, the header shows Signed in. Run a test import publishes a generated Claude Code marketplace with two uniquely named skills, downloads each one, and compares its files with the upload. The page shows Test import passed: published 2 generated skills, the downloaded files match, and both test skills were deleted. A mismatch fails the test and still deletes both skills. If a delete fails, the page lists the remaining IDs and offers Retry cleanup, which deletes only those IDs.

demoQueries.query: Import every skill from my team's plugin repository
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: After choosing the zip or folder, the page lists each discovered skill as create, update, unchanged, or invalid, with notes for skipped commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and remote plugin sources. Nothing is published until Import is clicked. Skills that share a name are unselected, and only one of them can be selected. Import publishes each selected skill once and shows created, new version, or failed for each. Importing the same plugin again shows every skill as unchanged.

codeAssets.description: TypeScript CLI that discovers skills in a Claude Code, Codex, or Agent Skills plugin and publishes each one through the Skills API

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Copy the importer app and its credential-free tests into a new directory. Sign-in uses the official @gleanwork/auth package.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Enter the project directory and install its dependencies.

steps.title: Run the fixture tests
steps.description: Run the tests without credentials or network access. They cover plugin discovery for each layout, zip handling, the app's session checks, and the Skills API workflow through the real SDK with MSW HTTP handlers. Passing them does not verify access to your Glean instance.

steps.title: Start the importer
steps.description: Start the app with your Glean backend URL. It opens the importer in your browser and prints an Open the importer link that includes this run's session key; use that link if no browser opens. Leave this terminal running while you use the app. If you do not know the backend URL, pass --email with your work email instead of --backend to discover it.

steps.title: Sign in with Glean
steps.description: Click **Sign in with Glean**. The app registers itself with your Glean instance and opens Glean's approval page in a new tab. Approve access, then return to the importer; the header changes to **Signed in**. Credentials are stored on this computer, outside the project.

steps.title: Or sign in from a terminal
steps.description: Use this instead of the button when the app cannot open a browser for you, for example on a remote machine. Open a new terminal, run the command, approve access in the browser, and reload the importer. To skip OAuth entirely, stop the app, copy .env.example to .env, set a user-scoped GLEAN_API_TOKEN with the SKILLS permission, and start it again.

steps.title: Run a test import
steps.description: Click **Run a test import**. The app publishes two generated skills, downloads each one, compares its files with the upload, and permanently deletes both. Success confirms sign-in and Skills API access before you import your own plugin.

steps.title: Choose your plugin
steps.description: Clone the plugin repository with your own Git credentials, or download it as a zip. A private repository stays private: the app reads it on this computer. Drop the zip on the page, or enter the folder path and click **Preview folder**. Use the repository root for a marketplace, or one plugin folder.

steps.title: Review and import
steps.description: Review the plan. Each skill is marked create, update (the name already exists), unchanged (its published files already match), or invalid. Untick any skill you do not want, then click **Import**. Skills are published as you, and an update adds a new version to a skill you own. Import again after the plugin changes; unchanged skills are skipped.

questions.prompt: What is your Glean backend URL, such as https://your-company-be.glean.com?

run.url: the Open the importer link printed by the server

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the plugin skill importer app. Ask for the user's Glean backend URL. Run credential-free fixture tests, then start the app with npm start -- --backend and the URL, and give the user the Open the importer link it prints, which includes the session key. The user signs in in the browser: the Sign in button runs the official glean-auth CLI from the pinned @gleanwork/auth package with the SKILLS scope and dynamic client registration. If the app cannot open a browser, the user can run npm run login -- --server-url with the URL in a new terminal and reload the page. Have the user run a test import, then choose the plugin zip or folder, review the plan, and click Import. The app reads marketplaces at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, and .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json, follows local plugin sources, reads skills paths from plugin.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, and .cursor-plugin/plugin.json, and scans each plugin's skills/ folder three levels deep. Without a manifest it scans skills/, .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/, and .cursor/skills/, then the whole tree. It uploads each distinct skill folder once as a ZIP, skips skills whose latest published files already match, never follows symbolic links, and reports remote plugin sources, commands, agents, hooks, and MCP servers instead of importing them. Never click Import for the user without their review, never supply Git credentials, never delete a skill the test import did not create, and never retry create automatically.
llmContext: Local web app (server.ts) on 127.0.0.1 with a per-run session key and Host check. Sign-in spawns glean-auth from pinned @gleanwork/auth (login --scopes SKILLS --server-url), the same as npm run login; createGleanTokenProvider supplies tokens. Use @gleanwork/api-client 0.20.16: skills.validate, list, retrieveContent (skip unchanged), and create; the test import also uses retrieve and delete. A same-name create by the same user adds a version; over a GitHub-imported skill it returns 409. Never retry create. Plugins are read in memory from a zip or folder; symbolic links are skipped. Only skills are imported. The test import deletes only captured IDs at version 1.1.

content.problem: Teams that share skills across agent harnesses usually keep them in a plugin repository: a Claude Code or Codex marketplace, a portable Agent Plugins package, or a folder of skills installed with npx skills. Those repositories are often private, and their skills are spread across several plugins. This recipe starts a small web app on your computer: sign in to Glean in the browser, drop in the plugin, review what it found, and publish every skill to Glean under your own account.
takeItFurther: Automate the import in CI after the plugin repository changes. Reuse planImport, selectSkills, and applyImport from src/workflow.ts with a user-scoped token in GLEAN_API_TOKEN, because the browser sign-in needs a person.
Use the GitHub import recipe for a public repository you want Glean to keep in sync from its source.
Use the skill publishing pipeline recipe to inspect versions and download a published bundle safely.

guardrails.title: Review before publishing
guardrails.rule: Choosing a plugin validates every bundle without saving it. Nothing is published until you click Import, and only the selected skills are uploaded.

guardrails.title: Publish as yourself
guardrails.rule: Each skill is created under the signed-in account. If you already own a skill with the same name, the upload adds a version to it. If someone else owns that name, you get your own skill with the same name. The plan shows existing owners before you publish.

guardrails.title: Never retry a create
guardrails.rule: Create runs once per skill with automatic retries off, because a request that timed out may still have saved the skill. Check the reported failures, then import again.

guardrails.title: Keep the app local
guardrails.rule: The app listens only on 127.0.0.1, answers only to its own host name, and requires the session key from the link it prints. Do not expose its port to a network.

guardrails.title: Read the plugin, never run it
guardrails.rule: The app reads files from the zip or folder in memory, rejects zip entries that escape the archive, and skips symbolic links. It never executes plugin scripts, hooks, or MCP servers.

limitations.title: Skills only
limitations.description: The Skills API stores skills. Plugin commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and settings are listed in the plan but not imported.

limitations.title: Remote plugin sources are not fetched
limitations.description: A marketplace entry that points to GitHub, a Git URL, npm, or an archive is reported, not downloaded. Clone or download that plugin and run the importer on its folder.

limitations.title: Not a sync
limitations.description: Imported skills are ordinary custom skills, not linked to the repository. Removing a skill from the plugin does not delete it from Glean. Import again to publish changes; skills whose files match their latest published version are skipped.

limitations.title: Names are global to your account
limitations.description: Glean has no plugin namespace, so two plugins with different skills of the same name conflict. The app leaves both unselected; select one, or rename one skill in the plugin.
